resources.name: scheduling-service
resources.description: Hospital scheduling-service — a GraphQL API (single endpoint POST /graphql). Tokens come from identity-service: run '0 · tokens → login (doctor)' once and every scheduling request pulls its Bearer token from that response. Role gate: DOCTOR/NURSE schedule, DOCTOR edits (and only the owner doctor). Host port 8085 in Docker, 8081 on the host.

resources.name: POST /auth/login  (doctor)  → 200
resources.description: Run this first. Every DOCTOR-authenticated request below reads accessToken from this response. If it 401s, register the user via the identity-service collection ('POST /users' as ADMIN, role DOCTOR).

resources.name: POST /auth/login  (nurse)  → 200
resources.description: A NURSE can schedule but not edit. Default points at 'smoke@hospital.local' (seeded by the identity smoke test); change nurse_email if needed.

resources.name: POST /auth/login  (admin)  → 200
resources.description: Only used by the 403 test — an ADMIN token is valid but the wrong role for scheduling.

resources.name: GET /graphql/schema  → 200 (SDL)
resources.description: The printed GraphQL schema as text. Public (permitAll).

resources.name: query _ping  → "ok"
resources.description: Smoke test. GraphQL requires at least one Query; scheduling exposes only mutations plus this _ping. Any authenticated token works.

resources.name: mutation scheduleAppointment  (DOCTOR) → SCHEDULED
resources.description: Persists the appointment (status SCHEDULED), then publishes a RabbitMQ reminder + a Kafka AppointmentCreated event. 'mutation editAppointment' reads the new id from this response.

resources.name: mutation scheduleAppointment  (NURSE) → SCHEDULED
resources.description: A NURSE may schedule. The 'not owner' error test edits this appointment (doctorId doc-2) with a DOCTOR token.

resources.name: mutation editAppointment  (status → CANCELLED)
resources.description: Edits the appointment from 'scheduleAppointment (DOCTOR)'. NOTE: succeeds only if that appointment's doctorId equals your JWT sub (the identity user id). Since the sample used doctorId 'doc-1', expect an ownership error — see 'scheduleAppointment (owner)' + 'editAppointment (as owner)' for the passing flow.

resources.name: mutation scheduleAppointment  (owner-linked)
resources.description: Schedules with doctorId = caller_doctor_id. Set that env var to your DOCTOR's identity user id (the JWT 'sub' — decode the token at jwt.io, or read it from identity-service). Then 'editAppointment (as owner)' can edit it.

resources.name: mutation editAppointment  (as owner) → updated
resources.description: Run right after 'scheduleAppointment (owner-linked)'. Same doctor, so the ownership check passes → 200 with the new scheduledAt. Also publishes a Kafka AppointmentUpdated event.

resources.name: mutation editAppointment  ({{ _.appointment_id }}, manual)
resources.description: Fallback: paste an id into the 'appointment_id' env var and run this (must be owned by your doctor).

resources.name: scheduleAppointment  (no token) → 401
resources.description: No Authorization header → HTTP 401 (rejected by the resource server before GraphQL runs).

resources.name: scheduleAppointment  (ADMIN token) → 403 / forbidden
resources.description: Valid token, wrong role. @PreAuthorize("hasAnyRole('DOCTOR','NURSE')") → GraphQL error with FORBIDDEN / access denied (HTTP 200 body with errors[]).

resources.name: scheduleAppointment  (past date) → validation error
resources.description: Domain rule: scheduledAt must be in the future. Expect errors[] with a BAD_REQUEST-style message and no data.

resources.name: editAppointment  (unknown id) → not found
resources.description: No appointment with that id → errors[] (not found).

resources.name: editAppointment  (not the owner doctor) → forbidden
resources.description: Run after 'scheduleAppointment (NURSE)' (doctorId doc-2). This DOCTOR token's sub != doc-2, so Appointment.edit rejects it → errors[] (only the owner doctor can edit).
